headline: Committee defers fiscal year 27 county budget item after emergency management review

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The emergency management administrator described work on 10 high-priority parcels covering 1,100 acres and a $1 million request to clear hazardous fuels. Bill 63 will be voted on when the committee takes up all the bills.
meeting.recap: The committee's one agenda item was the proposed fiscal year 27 budget for the County of Maui.[[0:03:11]] The emergency management administrator said 10 high-priority parcels covering 1,100 acres need work to lower wildfire risk.[[0:06:59]] The agency is asking for $1 million to clear hazardous fuels, meaning plants that can feed a fire.[[0:09:31]] He said funding for office space for emergency specialists on Molokaʻi and in Hāna exists, but no site is agreed on.[[0:15:47]] The chair said a presidential disaster declaration has been signed, which was needed for federal funding.[[0:36:48]] The administrator said the agency expects to move into its new emergency operations center in June.[[1:06:48]] Members were asked to send any more written questions by nine o'clock tomorrow morning.[[1:19:31]] The chair said the Hawaiian Cultural Restoration Revolving Fund holds $1.1 million.[[1:27:34]] The chair said Bill 63 will be voted on when the committee takes up all the bills.[[1:45:00]] The budget director said the bill's title needs a small fix to put Lahaina before Royal.[[1:51:45]] The budget item was deferred, meaning held for later, and the meeting was adjourned.[[2:05:04]]
meeting.next: The agency is working with procurement on a request for proposals for a strategic plan to define community resiliency hubs. The administrator said a presentation to the mayor is coming soon to bring the wildfire risk pieces together. The budget director said she is putting together a list of requested amendments.

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: A council member asked if the agency could fund getting perishable food from stores to people during outages.
issues.why: The member said East Maui was without electricity for about three days in the first Kona low storm.
issues.next: The administrator said he needed to check on the situation the member described.
issues.brief: The member thanked the agency for sending food supplies after the third day.[[#1]] The member said one store gives its perishable food to Red Cross to hand out at shelters.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: A presidential disaster declaration has been signed, which the chair said was needed for federal funding.
issues.why: The administrator said the declaration enables the Public Assistance program and a hazard mitigation program.
issues.next: The administrator said the agency and the Office of Recovery meet to decide when to hand off recovery work without a gap in service.
issues.brief: The administrator said the agency's main role under the declaration is cost recovery.[[#1]] He said the agency is still engaged in recovery from the two Kona storms.[[#2]] He said finishing a joint preliminary damage assessment with FEMA is a key milestone in recovery.[[#3]]
